title: Prefix popularity simulator, TTL slicing, and safe rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible simulator and runbook to automatically recommend per-prefix TTL slices and cache key shapes, and to apply those recommendations safely with staged rollouts and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers the simulator spec, offline backtests, recommended policy templates (TTL quantiles, per-prefix caps), and an operational playbook for safe apply and rollback.

Background: Current KV prefix caching is conservative: single global TTL and coarse policy results in missed cache opportunities for stable prefixes and excess cache holding for high-churn prefixes. Past experiments (see dependencies) showed meaningful token savings when TTLs are tuned by prefix popularity, but naive rollout increased tail latency under certain workloads. We need a system that: 1) quantifies likely hit-rate uplift and cost reduction per prefix, 2) produces conservative candidate configs with risk estimates, and 3) applies them safely with observable rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Simulator can ingest 30, 60, 90-day request traces, model per-prefix arrivals (configurable distributions), and output expected hit-rate, cost delta, and 95th/99th latency impact per policy.
2) Generate recommendation payloads: {prefix, recommended_TTL_ms, eviction_weight, max_entries} in JSONL that a downstream config-apply service can consume.
3) Offline backtest demonstrates >=10% token cost reduction for at least 25% of prefixes without >1% regression in 95th latency across aggregate traffic.
4) Automated rollout playbook exists with canary stages, automated rollback triggers, and a manual override.
5) Unit/integration tests and a small canary run (customer-segmented) completed and documented.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2w): Simulator prototype - parsers for request traces, basic arrival models (Poisson, renewal processes), TTL policy evaluator, per-prefix popularity estimator.
Phase 2 (2w): Backtester - run candidate policies across historical traces, produce per-prefix risk scores and uplift estimates, add heatmap visualizations.
Phase 3 (1w): Recommendation format and API contract + config-apply safe mode (staged percentage traffic, canary criteria).
Phase 4 (1w): Canary deployment to internal traffic, gather telemetry, tune rollback thresholds.
Phase 5 (1w): Documentation, runbook handoff, and dashboarding in Console.
simulation_spec:
Inputs: request traces (timestamp, prefix, token_count, latency_ms, route), model params (arrival_distribution_per_prefix, burstiness_alpha, base_miss_cost).
Model: For each prefix, fit a popularity curve (exponential smoothing + Pareto tail), estimate inter-arrival distribution; simulate cache with configurable TTL buckets (e.g., 1s, 5s, 30s, 5m, 1h) and record hit/miss sequences, re-fetch costs, token delta, and resulting downstream latency distribution (simple additive latency model).
Outputs: per-prefix table with: recommended_TTL, expected_hit_rate_change, expected_token_savings_pct, expected_latency_95_delta_ms, confidence_interval.
Backtest: replay at-sample and out-of-sample windows, compute uplift and false-positive risk (cases where simulated improvement translated to production degradation).
rollout_playbook:
1) Candidate selection: Only prefixes with >= X requests/day (default 100) and uplift CI lower bound > 3% considered.
2) Staged canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%; each stage 1 hour min and requires no rollback triggers.
3) Automatic rollback triggers: a) 95th latency for affected routes increases > 2x baseline or > 100ms absolute, b) error rate increase > 0.2pp, c) token cost savings < 0 after stage (indicates mis-simulation).
4) Safe-apply flags: dry_run (no writes), shadow_apply (mirror path to measure), safe_mode (apply but with TTL cap per prefix), emergency_cutover (instant global revert).
5) Post-apply: 24h monitoring window with regression dashboard, daily backfill comparison, and postmortem template if rollback occurs.
metrics:
Primary: token_savings_pct (aggregate), cost_savings_usd_estimated, cache_hit_rate_delta (per-prefix and aggregate).
Safety: route_95th_latency_delta_ms, route_error_rate_delta, request_timeout_rate, rollback_events_count.
Observability: per-stage snapshot histograms for latency and hit-rate, and a changelog of applied recommendations with hashes.
Success targets: >=10% token reduction on targeted prefixes with <1% overall 95th latency regression after 30d.
open_questions:
- Which production traces are permitted for simulator (PII concerns)? (security to confirm)
- Default minimum sample size for fitting prefix popularity? (currently 100 requests/day)
- Should TTLs be suggested as quantized buckets or continuous ms values? Quantized simplifies kernel behavior but may lose granularity.
- Integration point: will config-apply be pushed through Console rollout APIs or a new /admin/kv-policies endpoint?
